extraction.name: Instruction-Following Evaluation for Large Language Models (IFEval)
extraction.description: IFEval is a benchmark designed to evaluate the instruction-following ability of large language models (LLMs) using a set of prompts containing verifiable instructions. The benchmark focuses on 'verifiable instructions'—instructions that can be objectively verified for compliance, such as 'write in more than 400 words' or 'mention the keyword AI at least 3 times'. The dataset consists of 541 prompts, each containing one or more verifiable instructions, and evaluates the ability of models like GPT-4 and PaLM 2 to follow these instructions accurately. The benchmark aims to provide an easy-to-reproduce, unbiased, and automatic evaluation method for LLMs.
extraction.creator: Jeffrey Zhou, Tianjian Lu, Swaroop Mishra, Siddhartha Brahma, Sujoy Basu, Yi Luan, Denny Zhou, Le Hou
extraction.citeAs: Zhou, J., Lu, T., Mishra, S., Brahma, S., Basu, S., Luan, Y., Zhou, D., & Hou, L. (2023). Instruction-Following Evaluation for Large Language Models. arXiv preprint arXiv:2311.07911.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was constructed by identifying 25 types of verifiable instructions and generating 541 prompts, each containing one or more verifiable instructions. Prompts were synthesized through a four-step process: generating base prompts with verifiable instructions, using few-shot prompting to identify illogical prompts, rephrasing prompts to increase diversity, and manually checking and editing the rephrased prompts.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data consists of prompts and responses generated by LLMs (e.g., GPT-4 and PaLM 2) in response to the prompts. The prompts are designed to include verifiable instructions such as length constraints, keyword frequency, and structural requirements.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: The prompts were scraped in November 2023 (GPT-4) and August 2023 (PaLM 2).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Prompts were preprocessed to ensure they contained verifiable instructions. The preprocessing involved generating base prompts, filtering illogical prompts, rephrasing for diversity, and manual editing to ensure clarity and correctness.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The dataset includes annotations for instruction-following accuracy, with metrics such as strict and loose accuracy scores. Annotations were generated by verifying whether responses followed the verifiable instructions in the prompts.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The annotation analysis involves computing instruction-following accuracy scores (strict and loose) to evaluate the performance of LLMs. The analysis also includes identifying false negatives and positives in the verification process.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: Each prompt contains one or more verifiable instructions, and the responses are evaluated for compliance with these instructions.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: The verification process uses simple heuristics and programming to check if responses follow the verifiable instructions. Transformations (e.g., removing markdown tags, first/last lines) are applied to reduce false negatives.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset is released as part of the IFEval benchmark, with code and data available on GitHub. Future work includes expanding the diversity and quantity of verifiable instructions and extending the benchmark to multi-modal use cases.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset aims to improve the evaluation of LLMs by providing an objective and reproducible method for assessing instruction-following ability. This can enhance the reliability and safety of LLMs in real-world applications.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset focuses on verifiable instructions, which may not capture the full range of subjective or ambiguous instructions that LLMs encounter in real-world scenarios. The benchmark may also be biased toward the types of instructions included in the dataset.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited to verifiable instructions and does not cover subjective or ambiguous instructions. The benchmark may not fully capture the instruction-following ability of LLMs in real-world applications. Additionally, the dataset is static and may not reflect evolving instruction-following capabilities.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The dataset is designed for evaluating the instruction-following ability of LLMs. It can be used for training, testing, and validating LLMs, as well as for comparing the performance of different models. The benchmark provides a standardized and scalable approach to evaluation.
